questions.question: What is the correct substitution for the word 'screw' in the idiom 'Hit the screw on the head'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct idiom is** 'Hit the nail on the head'.**
 
• It means to say something that is exactly right (ऐसी बात कहना जो बिलकुल सही हो).
 
• Hence, the correct substitution for the word** 'screw' **in the idiom 'Hit the screw on the head' is** 'nail'.**

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Nail***.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select "No substitution required".

She __prepares an unique__ dish in the cooking competition and won it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. prepared a unique .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses the past tense **"won"**, so the verb **"prepare" **should also be in the **past tense (prepared)** to maintain tense consistency.
 
• The article **"a"** should be used before the word **"unique"** because "unique" starts with a **consonant sound**.

Correct sentence: *She **prepared a unique** dish in the cooking competition and won it*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consistency in Tense:**

 
 
• Ensure that all verbs in the sentence agree in tense to maintain clarity and coherence.
 
• Example: She prepared (past) a unique dish and won (past) the competition.
 
 
 
• **Article Usage:**
 
 
• Use "a" before words that begin with a consonant sound, and "an" before words that begin with a vowel sound.
 
• Example: a unique (consonant sound), an apple (vowel sound).

• **Cleft** (दरार): Split or severed.
 
 
• **Example:** The rock was cleft in two by the powerful earthquake.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

Work in this office is done in the ________ way.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. least efficient .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **comparing **the **efficiency **of work done in the office.
 
• When making **comparisons**, especially with **adjectives**, we use the **comparative degree** (e.g., less efficient) or the **superlative degree** (e.g., least efficient).
 
• Since the sentence is indicating the **lowest degree of efficiency**, the correct form to use is the **superlative degree (least)**.
 
• Among the given options, **"least efficient"** is the superlative form and correctly completes the sentence.

Correct sentence: *Work in this office is done in the **least efficient** way*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• **Usage:** Used to compare two entities.
 
• **Example:** This method is less efficient than the other one.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare more than two entities and indicate the highest or lowest degree.
 
• **Example: **This is the least efficient method of all.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I have lived with my parents / in Mumbai / in a residential flat / yet two years.

options.text: I have lived with my parents

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **yet two years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a **present perfect continuous tense**, which is used to show that something started in the past and has continued up until now.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"for two years"** instead of **"yet two years"**.
 
• Using "yet" in this context is incorrect; **"for"** is the appropriate preposition to indicate the duration of time.

Correct sentence: *I have lived with my parents in Mumbai in a residential flat **for** two years*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + have/has + been + verb(+ing).
 
• **Example:** She has been working here for five years.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that started in the past and are still continuing or were happening recently.
 
 
 
• **Common Error:**
 
 
• Using incorrect prepositions for time duration. For example, **"since"** is used with specific **points in time**, and **"for"** is used with **periods of time**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **abler**.

__
 
• The word **"ablest" **is **incorrectly **used in the given sentence. The sentence is comparing the ability of advocates, so a **comparative form** should be used.
 
• Among the options, **"abler"** is the correct **comparative **form of "able".
 
• Option 1 "more able" is also a comparative form but "abler" is preferred in this context.
 
• Option 3 "the ablest" and option 4 "most ablest" are **superlative forms** and do not fit the context of the sentence.

Correct sentence: *We have perhaps never seen an **abler** series of advocates than these ten standing in a row*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Form:**

 
 
• Used to compare differences between two objects (larger, smaller, faster, higher).
 
• Example: She is** taller** than her brother.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Form:**
 
 
• Used to describe an object that is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest).
 
• Example: She is the** tallest** girl in the class.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **and an hyena**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The article **"an"** is used before words that start with a vowel sound, while **"a"** is used before words that start with a consonant sound.
 
• In the given sentence, the word **"hyena"** starts with a consonant sound **"h"**, so the correct article to use is **"a"**.

Correct sentence: *A fox and **a** hyena were spotted in the animal reserve*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles "a" and "an":**

 
 
• **"A":** Used before words that begin with a consonant sound. Example: a car, a university.
 
• **"An":** Used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Example: an apple, an hour.
 
 
 
• **Common Mistakes:**
 
 
• Incorrect: an university (since "university" starts with a consonant sound).
 
• Correct: a university.

• **Example:** This book is **thicker** than that one. / This task is **more complex** than the previous one.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Adjective + est (for short adjectives) or most + Adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example: **This is the **tallest** building in the city. / She is the **most talented** artist in the group.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe an object that is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest).
